output.brief: Store 14's shrink rise is not yet shown to be a real change in losses. The figures are interim estimates extrapolated from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across the chain, about half of two-quarter interim rises of this size were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full counts have been stable at 1.5–1.8%. The rise is also spread across 61 of 74 product classes, and department sales mix was stable. That does not point to one cause. The shoplifting log counts are unreliable as a trend: the incident app launched chain-wide on 1 April, and recorded incidents rose chain-wide while chain shrink stayed flat. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and showed cardboard bale runs, not theft. Self-checkout and footfall coincide in time with the rise, but that does not show cause. My recommendation is to keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and decline Regional Operations' proposal to skip it. Hold off on pulling the lanes, hiring a guard, or taking any action against the night stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Extra cycle counts add little. Confidence is moderate to high on the action and lower on the individual causes.
